snapshotNote: Researched 2026-07-12 from official sources (NJ Courts, NJ Legislature statute database; Justia used only as locator/mirror of the official NJ Revised Statutes text — see LEGAL-RESEARCH-METHOD.md). Nothing here is APPROVED; counsel review is required before any client-facing legal use.

records.proposition: N.J.S.A. 2A:34-2 enumerates causes for divorce from the bond of matrimony, including (a) adultery; (b) willful and continued desertion for 12 or more months; (c) extreme cruelty (no complaint until 3 months after the last act, except for defendant's counterclaim); (d) separation for 18 or more consecutive months with no reasonable prospect of reconciliation; (e) addiction/habitual drunkenness for 12+ consecutive months; (f) institutionalization for mental illness for 24+ consecutive months; (g) imprisonment for 18+ consecutive months after marriage; (h) deviant sexual conduct; (i) irreconcilable differences for six months causing breakdown of the marriage.
records.authorityName: Causes for divorce from bond of matrimony
records.officialSource: New Jersey Revised Statutes, NJ Legislature statute database (lis.njleg.state.nj.us); text verified via Justia mirror of 2025 NJ Revised Statutes: https://law.justia.com/codes/new-jersey/title-2a/section-2a-34-2/
notes: NJ Legislature deep links are session-based; confirm text against the official database before approval.

records.proposition: N.J.S.A. 2A:34-2.1 enumerates causes for dissolution of a civil union (amended L.2006, c.103).
records.authorityName: Dissolution of a civil union, causes

records.proposition: N.J.S.A. 2A:34-8 states Superior Court jurisdiction over divorce/dissolution actions; N.J.S.A. 2A:34-10 sets residence requirements: a party must be a bona fide NJ resident when the cause arose and continuing, and for all causes other than adultery, one party must have been a bona fide NJ resident for at least one year before commencement (or one year of residence after the cause arose).
records.authorityName: Jurisdiction in divorce proceedings; service of process; residence requirements
records.officialSource: NJ Legislature statute database; text verified via Justia mirror (2025): https://law.justia.com/codes/new-jersey/title-2a/section-2a-34-10/
notes: Application to any specific facts is an attorney determination.

records.proposition: N.J.S.A. 2A:34-23 ('Alimony, maintenance') governs alimony/maintenance and related relief in matrimonial actions, including enumerated statutory factors and alimony types; equitable-distribution-related factor provisions are codified in the 2A:34-23 family of sections.

records.proposition: The Prevention of Domestic Violence Act of 1991, N.J.S.A. 2C:25-17 et seq. (short title at 2C:25-17; definitions at 2C:25-19), is New Jersey's statutory framework for domestic-violence protection, handled in the Family Part FV docket.
records.authorityName: Prevention of Domestic Violence Act of 1991

records.proposition: New Jersey's Uniform Child Custody Jurisdiction and Enforcement Act is codified at N.J.S.A. 2A:34-53 et seq. (short title 2A:34-53; definitions 2A:34-54) and governs interstate child-custody jurisdiction and enforcement.

records.proposition: New Jersey's Uniform Interstate Family Support Act provisions (e.g., N.J.S.A. 2A:4-30.133, continuing exclusive jurisdiction to modify child support) govern interstate support matters; the Judiciary maintains interstate-support rule guidance.
records.officialSource: NJ Legislature statute database; section caption verified via Justia mirror (2024): https://law.justia.com/codes/new-jersey/title-2a/section-2a-4-30-133/ ; Judiciary guidance: https://www.njcourts.gov/attorneys/rules-of-court/interstate-support
notes: [needs cite check] — exact first section of the 2016 UIFSA codification range not independently confirmed this pass.

records.proposition: New Jersey child-support guidelines are set out in Rules of Court Appendix IX (IX-A 'Considerations in the Use of Child Support Guidelines'; IX-B sole-parenting worksheet guidance), updated by annual Supreme Court order — most recently the order adopting updating amendments to Appendices IX-A, IX-B, IX-E and IX-H effective June 1, 2026.
records.authorityName: NJ Rules of Court, Appendix IX-A / IX-B (Child Support Guidelines)
records.section: Appendix IX-A, IX-B (and annual updating orders)
notes: Guideline schedules change annually — the snapshot MUST be re-verified each cycle.
No support calculator is implemented in this build.

records.proposition: The Family Part Case Information Statement (CIS) is the sworn financial-disclosure form for Family Part matters, prescribed as Appendix V to the NJ Rules of Court and published by the Judiciary as form CN 10482.
records.authorityName: Family Part Case Information Statement (Appendix V; CN 10482)
records.section: Rules of Court Appendix V; form CN 10482
notes: Form revision date to be confirmed on the PDF before form-mapping approval — [needs cite check].

records.proposition: The Confidential Litigant Information Sheet (CN 10486) is required to be filed in all dissolution (FM) and non-dissolution (FD) matters per Judiciary notice; it carries confidential party identifiers.
notes: Treat all CLIS-mapped intake fields as sensitive.

records.proposition: The NJ Family Practice Division identifies family docket types including FM (dissolution/divorce), FD (non-dissolution custody/support), and FV (domestic violence / VASPA), among others (FN, FC, FG, FA, FL, FJ, FF, FO).
records.authorityName: Family Practice Division — case types and docket codes

records.proposition: The Judiciary's divorce self-help materials describe the filing steps (summons/complaint, county filing, $300 filing fee plus $25 where custody/parenting time is requested, 30-day service), and settlement programs (mediation, arbitration, Early Settlement Panels).
notes: Fees change; re-verify before client-facing display — fee figures are NOT rendered to clients in this build.

records.proposition: The Judiciary publishes a post-judgment motion kit for Family Part matters (CN 10483, revised 08/06/2020) and self-help guidance for post-judgment motions (enforcement/modification).
notes: Check for a later revision before mapping approval — [needs cite check].

records.proposition: Practice in the Chancery Division, Family Part is governed by Part V of the New Jersey Rules of Court, with family-specific appendices (V — CIS; IX — child support); the Supreme Court's 2025 omnibus rule amendment order is the most recent general amendment cycle located.
records.authorityName: NJ Rules of Court, Part V (Family Part) and Appendices
notes: Specific governing rule numbers (e.g., venue, CIS filing triggers) were [not found] in this pass and must be supplied by counsel review.

records.proposition: Non-dissolution (FD) cases cover custody, parenting time, and support outside divorce; the Judiciary provides FD filing self-help, and a Judiciary Special Committee on the Non-Dissolution (FD) Docket has proposed rule amendments (comments cycle 2025).
